Summarize Posterior Landscape Scales

Source: R/bayes_scale_methods.R
posterior_scales.Rd

Report the scale of each landscape predictor in projected map units, for every distinct combination of scale-formula covariates and groups, with its posterior uncertainty and the posterior mass outside the range of the prepared inputs.

Usage

posterior_scales(
  object,
  level = 0.95,
  draws = NULL,
  scale = c("distance", "log"),
  estimator = c("draws", "weighted")
)

Arguments

object

A fitted multiScale_bayes() object with posterior draws, from sampling or either approximation. A prepared object has no draws and gives an error.

level

Probability of the central posterior interval; default 0.95.

draws

Optional positive integer number of stored draws to use, taken at evenly spaced positions. The default NULL uses every stored draw. Fewer draws run faster and add simulation noise.

scale

"distance" (default) reports scales in projected map units. "log" reports natural log distances in those units. Log summaries avoid exponentiating very large distances, and their means and SDs stay finite under the default group-SD prior (see "Read means of long-tailed distances").

estimator

"draws" (default) summarizes the stored draws, for every method. "weighted" summarizes all retained production candidates of an importance-corrected fit with their normalized importance weights, which avoids the extra noise of resampling. It requires draws = NULL and a fit made with control = list(correction = "importance").

Value

A data frame with one row per landscape predictor and distinct combination of scale-formula covariates and groups.

  • covariate: the landscape predictor.

  • group: a label for the combination, such as "year=2021", or "shared" for a predictor with a single scale.

  • row: a representative observation row with that combination.

  • mean, median, sd, lower, upper: the posterior mean, median, and SD, and the limits of the central level credible interval. Values are in map units, or in log map units when scale = "log". For log summaries, exp() of the median and the limits gives distances, but exp() of the mean gives a geometric mean, not the arithmetic mean distance.

  • p_below_min_D, p_above_max_D: the posterior probability that the scale lies below min_D or above max_D of the prepared inputs. These flag truncation and resolution limits. They are not evidence of a biological boundary.

mean and sd summarize a finite set of draws. A finite value does not show that the corresponding posterior moment exists. With estimator = "weighted", quantiles are empirical inverse-CDF quantiles of the weighted candidates and sd is the SD of that finite weighted population.

Read annual scales after partial pooling

For a scale formula such as ~1 + (1 | year), each row describes one fitted year's scale after partial pooling. Its median is not a separately estimated annual value. The shared log-scale intercept describes a population median, which differs from the arithmetic mean of the annual scales. Intervals are conditional on the likelihood, the priors, the maps, and the binning. With scale = "log", sd measures uncertainty in one year's log distance. It differs from the between-year SD reported in summary(object)$group_sd.

Read means of long-tailed distances

A random scale effect is \(\tau z\), with standard-normal z and a half-normal tau whose prior scale is s (scale_group_sd). Its prior exponential moment of order r exists only when \(r s < 1\). The default scale_group_sd = 0.5 therefore places the variance of annual distances at the boundary where it becomes infinite, and scale_group_sd >= 1 also allows an infinite arithmetic mean distance. The binned likelihood can keep these tails, because very large distances approach uniform weighting within the extracted neighborhood. Report medians and interval limits for distances, and use scale = "log" when you need means and SDs.

Summarize importance-corrected fits directly

For a fit made with correction = "importance", estimator = "weighted" summarizes the retained candidate population with its normalized weights instead of the resampled draws. Both target the same posterior. The weighted version avoids multinomial resampling noise, but it neither raises the importance effective sample size nor recovers a posterior region the candidates missed. Candidates with zero weight are dropped. The cautions about infinite distance moments still apply.

plot.multiScaleR_bayes() uses the weighted estimator by default for corrected fits, while this function and summary() default to the draws. Request estimator = "weighted" in both to keep a table and a plot consistent.

Weighted summaries are only as precise as the candidate population. importance_max in the control list of multiScale_bayes() is a cap, and a population that passes its checks at a smaller size stops there. To require more candidates for precise quantiles, raise importance_min as well, as in control = list(correction = "importance", importance_min = 65536, importance_max = 131072). Larger populations cost more and do not guarantee a chosen quantile error. Check the retained count in fit$diagnostics$candidates, and compare independently seeded fits.

See also

multiScale_bayes(), multiScaleR_bayes, plot.multiScaleR_bayes(), predict_scales(), diagnose_bayes_scales(), kernel_dist(); vignette("v13-bayesian-scales", package = "multiScaleR") and vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

example <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bayesian-annual-example.rds",
  package = "multiScaleR"))
fit <- example$fits$pooled  # compact draws from an annual-scale NUTS fit
annual <- posterior_scales(fit)
annual[c("group", "median", "lower", "upper", "p_below_min_D")]
#>       group   median    lower    upper p_below_min_D
#> 1 year=2021 173.0828 39.08530 431.8495        0.1935
#> 2 year=2022 173.7422 41.71146 423.5986        0.1840
#> 3 year=2023 143.6104 34.01918 376.3533        0.2665
#> 4 year=2024 175.0161 41.81391 441.1051        0.1665
#> 5 year=2025 155.9366 49.68400 373.9298        0.1870
# Sigma for each year in meters, with central 95% credible intervals.
# Part of each posterior lies below min_D (100 m, one raster cell).

posterior_scales(fit, scale = "log")[c("group", "mean", "sd")]
#>       group     mean        sd
#> 1 year=2021 5.091107 0.6186922
#> 2 year=2022 5.104301 0.6013087
#> 3 year=2023 4.928907 0.5995917
#> 4 year=2024 5.122512 0.5886036
#> 5 year=2025 5.016202 0.5348244
# The log-distance SD measures uncertainty in one year's scale, not the
# variation among years.

# Convert the median sigma to the radius holding 90% of the kernel weight
kernel_dist(sigma = annual$median[1], kernel = "gaussian")
#> [1] 371.43
